title: Panna Cotta
subtitle: Italian cream jelly
excerpt: Set cream sweetened with sugar and flavoured with vanilla, unmoulded and served with a sharp fruit compote. Silky, light, and very easy to make ahead.

recipe.sourceNotes: Panna cotta (cooked cream) is a dessert from Piedmont in Northern Italy. It became widely known outside Italy in the 1990s and is now a standard of Italian restaurant menus worldwide.

recipeTools.notes: Four 150 ml ramekins or dariole moulds.

content.text: Panna cotta is sweetened cream set with gelatine and flavoured with vanilla. It should tremble when shaken and barely hold its shape when unmoulded. The texture is meant to be barely set, softer than jelly, almost liquid at the centre. It sets overnight in the fridge and takes a few hours at minimum.
Lightly oil the inside of four 150 ml ramekins with a flavourless oil. Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes until soft.
Warm the cream, sugar, and vanilla pod and seeds in a saucepan over a medium heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the cream is just steaming. Do not let it boil. Remove from the heat.
Lift the soaked gelatine leaves from the water, squeezing out the excess water, and add them to the hot cream. Stir until completely dissolved. Remove the vanilla pod.
Strain through a fine sieve into a jug. Pour into the prepared ramekins. Leave to cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.

To unmould, run a finger around the edge to loosen, place a plate on top, and invert firmly. If it does not release, briefly dip the base of the ramekin in warm water. Serve with a sharp berry compote or crushed raspberries.
